Looking at this question about the ColabFold prediction for HcKCR1 (a channelrhodopsin from Hyphochytrium catenoides), I need to consider which of the 7 transmembrane helices would typically have a poor prediction.

In channelrhodopsin structure predictions using homology-based methods like ColabFold, TM7 is often the most challenging helix to predict accurately. This is because TM7 in channelrhodopsins tends to be shorter, more flexible, and less well-conserved compared to the other transmembrane helices, leading to lower confidence (pLDDT) scores in structure predictions.

[ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
